text:
**Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a US flight, but only in your carry-on, never in checked bags.**

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each. To convert, divide mAh by 1000 and multiply by the voltage ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- A typical 20,000 mAh bank is rated at 3.7 V, so 20 Ah × 3.7 V ≈ **74 Wh**, well under the limit. Check the Wh figure printed on your bank if there is one.
- Banks between 101 and 160 Wh need airline approval, with a maximum of two per person. Anything over 160 Wh is not allowed on passenger aircraft ([FAA PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank)).

**Rules to follow**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare lithium batteries and power banks are prohibited in checked baggage.
- **Gate-checked bags.** If your carry-on gets checked at the gate, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over the ports, so nothing shorts it out.
- **No damaged or recalled batteries.** Swollen or damaged units shouldn't fly.
- **Airline limits.** Some airlines set stricter limits, such as a cap on the number of power banks, so check your carrier's policy. IATA also advises this ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).
- **In flight.** Tell the crew right away if a battery gets hot, swells, or smokes.

**If you're shopping for one:** the Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W USB-C, about 74 Wh) is listed as airline-carry-on legal at $89.99 on [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). The listing's buy link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy through it. I haven't compared it against other models.
